answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen pricing despite the 18% mandate, making renegotiation unlikely to succeed. Memory_c2 demonstrates that moving to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—directly applicable to meeting the finance mandate. Memory_c4 shows negotiation can work when the vendor is willing, but the incumbent's refusal signals they hold the relationship differently. With 94% line utilization and no buffer, full immediate switch carries delivery risk. A small guarded test (partial volume allocation to verified low-cost vendor, retention of incumbent for safety buffer) mirrors the second-sourcing success in memory_c3 while capturing cost recovery. This preserves the option to scale if onboarding and quality hold, defers full cutover risk until the next cycle, and maintains partial incumbent relationship to protect the 6% buffer. The 14-day renewal window is tight but sufficient for a phased transition trial.
